question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

She is one of those (a)/ social workers who (b)/ has dedicated (c)/ their lives to the poor. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the pattern "one of those + plural noun + who / that", the relative pronoun refers to the plural noun ("social workers"), so the verb in the clause is plural. So "has dedicated" must be "have dedicated".

◦ Corrected sentence: She is one of those social workers who have dedicated their lives to the poor.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "She is one of those" is proper, with "one of those" followed by a plural noun.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "social workers who" is proper, with the relative pronoun "who" used for people.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "their lives to the poor." is proper, with the plural "their" agreeing with "workers" and "the poor" naming a group.

 

NOTE

 

• one of the students who are, one of those who have (plural verb in the clause); but the only one of the students who is (singular).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

There are (a)/ many reasons (b)/ why the project (c)/ have been delayed. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A verb agrees with its own subject. In "why the project have been delayed", the subject of the clause is the singular "the project", and the plural "reasons" in the main clause does not change it. So "have been delayed" must be "has been delayed".

◦ Corrected sentence: There are many reasons why the project has been delayed.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "There are" is proper, because the noun that follows, "many reasons", is plural.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "many reasons" is proper, with "many" followed by a plural noun.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "why the project" is proper, with "why" introducing the clause and "the project" as a specific project.

 

NOTE

 

• There are many reasons why the plan has failed; the verb of a clause agrees with the subject of that clause and not with a noun in the main clause.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Five hundred rupees (a)/ are a small (b)/ amount for (c)/ such a costly repair. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A sum of money, a period of time or a distance is treated as one unit and takes a singular verb. So "are a small" must be "is a small".

◦ Corrected sentence: Five hundred rupees is a small amount for such a costly repair.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Five hundred rupees" is proper, because "hundred" takes no "-s" after a number.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "amount for" is proper, with the correct preposition "for" after "amount".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "such a costly repair." is proper, with the pattern "such + a + adjective + noun".

 

NOTE

 

• Ten thousand rupees is a big sum, Five years is a long time, Three kilograms is enough (a measure treated as one unit takes a singular verb).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

To speak (a)/ the truth (b)/ are always (c)/ a mark of courage. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An infinitive (to + verb) used as a subject is singular and takes a singular verb. So "are always" must be "is always".

◦ Corrected sentence: To speak the truth is always a mark of courage.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "To speak" is proper, with the infinitive used as the subject.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "the truth" is proper, with "the" used before "truth" when a specific truth is meant.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "a mark of courage." is proper, with "a" before the consonant sound of "mark" and no article before "courage".

 

NOTE

 

• To err is human; Walking is good exercise (a gerund subject); What he said was true (a noun clause subject): all take a singular verb.

question:

Half of the (a)/ mangoes in the basket (b)/ were rotten. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

◦ Sentence as given: Half of the mangoes in the basket were rotten.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Half of the" is proper, with "half of" followed by a specific noun.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "mangoes in the basket" is proper, with a plural noun and "the basket" as a specific container.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "were rotten." is proper, with the plural verb "were" agreeing with "mangoes".

 

NOTE

 

• Half of the mangoes were (plural noun); Half of the milk was (uncountable noun).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Every boy (a)/ and every girl (b)/ in the school (c)/ have received a prize. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When two singular nouns are joined by "and" and each is preceded by "every" or "each", the verb is singular. So "have received" must be "has received".

◦ Corrected sentence: Every boy and every girl in the school has received a prize.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Every boy" is proper, because "every" is followed by a singular noun.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "and every girl" is proper, because "every" is again followed by a singular noun.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "in the school" is proper, with "the school" as a specific place.

 

NOTE

 

• Every boy and every girl has; Each teacher and each student is (singular verb).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

The scenery of (a)/ the Kashmir Valley (b)/ are breathtaking. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Scenery" is an uncountable noun and takes a singular verb. So "are breathtaking" must be "is breathtaking".

◦ Corrected sentence: The scenery of the Kashmir Valley is breathtaking.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The scenery of" is proper, with the uncountable noun "scenery" and "of" showing what it belongs to.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "the Kashmir Valley" is proper, with "the" used before the name of a valley.

 

• Option (d) No error — cannot be selected, because "are" in part (c) does not agree with the singular "scenery".

 

NOTE

 

• The scenery is, The weather was, The luggage is (uncountable nouns take a singular verb).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The peon looked (a)/ everywhere and finally (b)/ reported that (c)/ a bunch of keys were missing. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In "a bunch of keys", the subject is "a bunch" (singular), and the noun after "of" does not decide the verb. So "were missing" must be "was missing".

◦ Corrected sentence: The peon looked everywhere and finally reported that a bunch of keys was missing.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The peon looked" is proper, with a singular subject and the simple past verb "looked".

 

• Part (b) is correct — "everywhere and finally" is proper, with two adverbs joined by "and".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "reported that" is proper, with "that" introducing the noun clause.

 

NOTE

 

• A bunch of keys was, A pair of shoes is, A flock of birds was (the noun before "of" decides the verb).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

A pair of spectacles were (a)/ left on the bench (b)/ by an old man (c)/ yesterday evening. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In "a pair of + noun", the subject is "pair" (singular), so the verb is singular. So "A pair of spectacles were" must be "A pair of spectacles was".

◦ Corrected sentence: A pair of spectacles was left on the bench by an old man yesterday evening.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "left on the bench" is proper, with "on" used for a surface and "the bench" as a specific place.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "by an old man" is proper, with "an" used before the vowel sound of "old".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "yesterday evening." is proper, because "yesterday evening" takes no article or preposition.

 

NOTE

 

• A pair of scissors is (singular); The scissors are (plural, when "a pair of" is not used).

question:

The criteria (a)/ for selection (b)/ is clearly stated (c)/ in the notification. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

• Part (d) is correct — "in the notification." is proper, with "the notification" as a specific document.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

He is the only one (a)/ among the guests (b)/ who has visited Japan. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The sentence is grammatically correct. In "the only one … who", the relative pronoun refers to the singular "one", so the verb in the clause is singular. So "who has visited" is correct.

◦ Sentence as given: He is the only one among the guests who has visited Japan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "He is the only one" is proper, with "the" used before "only".

 

• Part (b) is correct — "among the guests" is proper, with "among" followed by a plural noun.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "who has visited Japan." is proper, with the singular verb "has" agreeing with "one" and no article before the name of a country.

 

NOTE

 

• the only one who has (singular); but one of the guests who have (plural).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

What the minister said were (a)/ completely false, (b)/ as the facts (c)/ later showed. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A noun clause beginning with "What" used as a subject is treated as singular and takes a singular verb. So "What the minister said were" must be "What the minister said was".

◦ Corrected sentence: What the minister said was completely false, as the facts later showed.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "completely false," is proper, with the adverb "completely" modifying the adjective "false".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "as the facts" is proper, with "as" introducing a clause and "the facts" as a plural subject.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "later showed." is proper, with the simple past tense "showed" and the adverb "later" correctly placed.

 

NOTE

 

• What he said was, What matters is, What you need is (a noun clause subject takes a singular verb).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Behind the old temple (a)/ stand a tall (b)/ banyan tree planted (c)/ a century ago. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In an inverted sentence (verb before the subject), the verb agrees with the real subject that comes after it. The real subject here is the singular "a tall banyan tree", so "stand" must be "stands".

◦ Corrected sentence: Behind the old temple stands a tall banyan tree planted a century ago.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Behind the old temple" is proper, with "behind" showing position and "the old temple" as a specific place.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "banyan tree planted" is proper, with the past participle "planted" describing the tree.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "a century ago." is proper, with "a" used before the consonant sound of "century".

 

NOTE

 

• Behind the house stands a tree, Here comes the bus, There lie two books (in an inverted sentence, the noun after the verb decides).

question:

• In "the rest of + noun", the verb agrees with the noun after "of". "Money" is uncountable, so the verb is singular. So "The rest of the money were" must be "The rest of the money was".

◦ Corrected sentence: The rest of the money was deposited in the bank on Monday, before the holiday.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "deposited in the bank" is proper, with "the bank" as a specific place.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "on Monday," is proper, with "on" used before a day of the week.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "before the holiday." is proper, with "the holiday" as a specific day.

 

NOTE

 

• The rest of the money was (uncountable noun); The rest of the students were (plural noun).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The project was (a)/ completed on time, (b)/ but a large amount of (c)/ money have been wasted. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

• "A large amount of" + an uncountable noun takes a singular verb. So "money have been wasted" must be "money has been wasted".

◦ Corrected sentence: The project was completed on time, but a large amount of money has been wasted.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The project was" is proper, with the singular verb "was" agreeing with "project".

 

• Part (b) is correct — "completed on time," is proper, because "on time" means "punctually" and takes no article.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "but a large amount of" is proper, because "amount" is used with an uncountable noun.

 

NOTE

 

• a large amount of money (uncountable), a large number of people (countable); A large amount of money has been spent.

question:

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

• Forty per cent of the employees have (plural noun); Forty per cent of the milk has (uncountable noun).

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence.

 

The students who was absent yesterday must submit a written note.

The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. were absent.

◦ Corrected sentence: The students who were absent yesterday must submit a written note.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "is absent" — this is a singular verb, and the present tense does not suit "yesterday".

 

• Option 2: "has been absent" — this is a singular verb, and the plural "students" needs a plural verb.

 

• Option 4: No improvement required — incorrect, because the singular "was" does not agree with the plural "students".

 

NOTE

 

• The students who were, The boy who was (the relative pronoun agrees with its antecedent).

question:

question:

question:

The main attraction of the fair were the magic shows and the folk dances.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. was.

• The verb agrees with the subject and not with the complement. The subject is the singular "attraction", so "were" must be "was", even though the complement "the magic shows and the folk dances" is plural.

◦ Corrected sentence: The main attraction of the fair was the magic shows and the folk dances.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "are" — this is a plural verb, and the subject "attraction" is singular.

 

• Option 3: "have been" — this is a plural verb, and the subject "attraction" is singular.

 

• Option 4: No improvement required — incorrect, because the plural "were" does not agree with the singular subject "attraction".

 

NOTE

 

• The main attraction was the shows (the verb agrees with the subject, not with the complement).

question:
